421: B is correct because AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed, serverless SFTP service, and using an internet-facing VPC endpoint with Elastic IP addresses lets a security group restrict access to only the trusted IP addresses, providing highly configurable security. Amazon EFS is serverless shared storage that scales automatically and delivers the high, consistent IOPS performance the SFTP workload needs, and it attaches directly to the Transfer Family endpoint. Unlike the S3-backed options, EFS preserves POSIX-style file and directory semantics, and EBS volumes cannot be attached to a Transfer Family endpoint at all.
422: D is correct because SQS queues the asynchronous requests and decouples ingestion from processing, absorbing batches of thousands of requests while tolerating models sitting idle for days or weeks. Deploying the models as ECS services runs them as long-lived containers that load the 1 GB of model data from S3 into memory once and reuse it across requests, avoiding the per-invocation startup penalty that Lambda would pay. AWS Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster and service copies driven by queue size scales out for large batches and scales in to minimize cost when usage is low.
423: A is correct because identity-based policies can be attached to IAM roles, where the permissions apply to any principal that assumes the role. B is correct because identity-based policies can also be attached to IAM groups, granting the permissions to every user in the group. IAM identity policies attach only to IAM users, groups, and roles; organizations enforce guardrails with service control policies, and ECS or EC2 resources receive permissions through service roles rather than directly attached identity policies.
424: B is correct because Reserved Instances provide the lowest cost for the frontend nodes that run continuously 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The backend nodes run only for short, variable periods, so Spot Instances offer the deep discounts that suit interruptible, scalable compute, with Auto Scaling replacing any interrupted instances. Spot for the always-on frontend would risk interruptions and SLA impact, making Reserved plus Spot the most cost-effective combination.
425: C is correct because the gp3 volume type delivers a 3,000 IOPS baseline and lets you provision IOPS independently of storage capacity, up to 16,000 IOPS, which covers the 15,000 IOPS peak at about 20% lower cost per GB than gp2. The io1 and io2 volume types support higher performance tiers but cost considerably more, making them less cost-effective for this IOPS level. gp3 is the standard choice for general-purpose workloads needing provisioned IOPS separate from volume size.
426: A is correct because AWS DataSync efficiently and securely moves the existing on-premises data into Amazon S3 over encrypted connections, resolving the storage capacity shortage. Enabling CloudTrail data events on the S3 bucket records object-level access operations, which satisfies the new regulation requiring audit access at all levels of the stored healthcare data. Snowcone and Storage Gateway are designed for edge or hybrid ongoing use rather than a one-time migration, and management events alone would not capture object-level access.
427: B is correct because Elastic Beanstalk natively supports Java applications on Apache Tomcat with a load-balanced, auto-scaling environment across multiple Availability Zones, delivering high availability with minimal operational effort. Rolling deployments keep the application available during updates, and Amazon RDS can provide the MySQL database. Deploying on Lambda does not fit the Tomcat application model, and manually building AMIs with launch templates and Auto Scaling involves far more administration overhead.
428: B is correct because a Lambda execution role is an IAM role that trusts the Lambda service, is assumed automatically by the function at runtime, and grants read and write access to the DynamoDB table through short-lived temporary credentials. This is the most secure approach because no long-lived access keys exist to leak or manage. The options that create IAM users and store access keys in environment variables or Parameter Store all risk credential exposure.
429: D is correct because in IAM policy evaluation an explicit Deny always overrides an Allow, so the Deny statement blocks ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances in the us-east-1 Region unless the user authenticates with MFA, while the Allow statement permits any other Amazon EC2 action in that Region. The Allow is scoped to us-east-1, so the permissions do not extend to all Regions. Statement order does not matter in IAM; each request is evaluated against all statements before access is decided.
430: B is correct because a Lambda function triggered by S3 event notifications converts the .csv files into images immediately upon upload and stores them back in the bucket, making them available as soon as possible with no idle compute cost. C is correct because transitioning the .csv files to S3 Glacier one day after upload minimizes storage cost for data that is only retrieved twice a year for ML training and audits planned weeks in advance, while expiring the image files after 30 days removes them as soon as they become irrelevant. Glacier's low storage price and scheduled retrieval model fit this access pattern, whereas Standard-IA or One Zone-IA cost more for rarely accessed data, and keeping images in Reduced Redundancy Storage never expires them.
431: B is correct because ElastiCache for Redis supports sorted sets that can compute and cache a top-10 scoreboard in near real time even with many concurrent players. Redis also provides persistence through snapshots and backups, which enables the game to be stopped and restored while preserving the current scores. Memcached offers no persistence, CloudFront caching is not suited to rapidly changing dynamic data, and an RDS read replica would introduce replication lag for frequently updated scores.
432: B is correct because Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed service for building, training, and deploying ML models with the least operational overhead. Amazon QuickSight is a serverless business intelligence service that can integrate with the ML output and visualize the augmented data directly in dashboards. The alternatives either require managing EC2 instances from a Marketplace AMI or attempt to use tools that are not purpose-built for ML model training.
433: C is correct because a service control policy in AWS Organizations enforces preventative guardrails across all accounts in the organization, so it can deny tag modification except by authorized principals in both production and nonproduction accounts. SCPs are the native mechanism for restricting actions on cost allocation tags in a multi-account environment. Config rules and CloudWatch logs only detect or record changes after they occur, and a CloudTrail trail is for logging, not prevention.
434: A is correct because an Auto Scaling group and load balancer already running in the disaster recovery Region create a warm standby, so failover requires only a DNS switch and produces the least downtime. Configuring the DynamoDB table as a global table continuously replicates the data to the DR Region so it is current at failover. Route 53 DNS failover automates the traffic shift to the DR load balancer, whereas creating resources on demand with CloudFormation incurs longer recovery times, and a custom CloudWatch alarm with Lambda adds unnecessary complexity.
435: A is correct because a Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device easily transports the 20 TB of data within the two-week window, while AWS DMS with ongoing replication captures changes made during the transfer to minimize downtime. This hybrid bulk-transfer plus change-data-capture approach is the most cost-effective for this timeline. Snowmobile is designed for exabyte-scale migrations and is far more expensive, and a dedicated Direct Connect link takes weeks to provision.
436: A is correct because making the existing RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance larger vertically scales it to handle the increased workload without adding any new infrastructure, which the requirement demands. Buying reserved DB instances for the total workload provides a significant discount compared with on-demand pricing for the now larger, steady-state instance. Multi-AZ or an additional DB instance adds infrastructure and cost without addressing the compute and capacity need.
437: B is correct because AWS WAF can be associated with the ALB, and a rate-based rule automatically blocks requests from any source IP that exceeds a configured threshold within a five-minute window, which directly counters the high request rate from illegitimate systems with changing IP addresses. Rate limiting affects only the abusive sources, so the impact on legitimate users is minimal. Inspector is for vulnerability scanning, GuardDuty is threat detection, and network ACLs cannot perform rate limiting for dynamic IP addresses.
438: D is correct because creating an encrypted snapshot and sharing it with the auditor's own AWS account gives the auditor an independent copy of the database without exposing network access to the private subnet. Granting the auditor access to the KMS customer managed key allows the snapshot to be decrypted securely in the auditor's account. Sharing long-lived IAM user credentials or exporting loose text files to S3 would be less secure and harder to audit.
439: A is correct because associating an additional IPv4 CIDR block with the existing VPC and creating new subnets from it expands the address space with the least operational overhead, since no new connectivity infrastructure or route changes are required. Existing resources continue to run while new workloads launch in the new subnets using the new CIDR. The other options require building and managing a second VPC plus peering, Transit Gateway, or VPN connections with extra routing and cost.
440: A is correct because an RDS for MySQL DB snapshot can be migrated directly into a MySQL-compatible Aurora DB cluster using the migrate snapshot feature, which creates the new DB instance from the final snapshot without any intermediate steps. C is correct because a mysqldump backup can be uploaded to Amazon S3 and then imported into Aurora MySQL, which natively supports loading data from text files stored in an S3 bucket. Neither backup requires DMS, and uploading an RDS snapshot to S3 is not a valid path since snapshots migrate directly.
